dimensions.note: A timeline's scale is a decision about what the spatial dimension is allowed to claim. Proportional when the gaps carry meaning the reader needs; ordinal when only order matters. Ordinal applied to duration-critical data fails silently, which makes it the more dangerous error for an automated system: nothing about the plate looks broken.
dimensions.evidence: Full text obtained during SUE-627 research; the paper treats scale, representation and layout as independent design-space axes.

dimensions.note: A mixed scale inside one plate with no visible seam is the least recoverable failure, because the reader has no way to know which segments are measured.
Bears on visual/body-infographic and visual/analytical-graphic wherever a plate carries progression or chronology.
The design space is orthogonal to how much a single plate should carry.

strengths: Turns 'timeline' from one shape into an explicit scale decision with a stated failure mode for each direction.
weaknesses: Academic taxonomy rather than a rendered editorial artifact; it says nothing about visual restraint or mobile type floors.
notes: Used as a design-space vocabulary. Craft evidence only.
